title: Battery Handling and Dangerous Goods Logistics
summary: Rules for shipping and receiving returned warranty battery packs using approved dangerous-goods carriers and incident handling for standard parcel arrivals.

infobox.Topic: Battery Handling and Dangerous Goods Logistics
infobox.Scope: Warranty battery returns from bike shops

body:
Battery handling and dangerous goods logistics govern the transport and receipt of lithium battery packs returned under warranty. Returned battery packs must travel strictly through certified transport channels to prevent safety hazards and regulatory breaches. Receiving staff must follow strict containment and logging protocols if non-compliant shipments arrive at Northbridge facilities.

## Transit and carrier requirements

Returned battery packs from bike shops under warranty must be shipped exclusively via approved dangerous-goods carriers and never through ordinary postal or parcel networks [^r1]. 

## Non-compliant consignments and incident protocol

If a returned battery pack arrives via standard parcel transit, the safety officer must be notified immediately and an incident logged before opening the consignment [^r2].

## See also

* [[sop-sal-002|SOP-SAL-002 Warranty Claims from Bike Shops]]
* [[pol-ret-006|POL-RET-006 Returns Policy]]

r1.section: Common mistakes by bike shops and internal staff
r1.loc_text: p. 3, Common mistakes by bike shops and internal staff
r1.quote: Paragraph 5.3 requires bike shops to return packs exclusively via the approved dangerous-goods carrier.

r2.section: What to do when something does not look right
r2.loc_text: p. 4, What to do when something does not look right
r2.quote: If a battery pack arrives through an ordinary parcel carrier instead of the dangerous-goods route, notify the safety officer immediately and log the incident on the claim file before unpacking the consignment.
